1.why: Nothing separates five parallel noun phrases; picked the one that ties to the batch's recurring cast-provenance thread (marbles the casts were taken from).

2.why: Only option that concedes the trend and then refuses a single cause, the same concede-then-qualify shape that recurs across this batch's record items (24, 18).

3.why: Options split into cash, nothing, and two in-kind payments; picked the in-kind one because other items imply she was paid, but poorly.

4.why: Two options (A, B) address measurement precision and three address scope; no structural way to separate A from B.

5.why: A and C are an impression/explanation pair; picked the impression, which is the usual stem target, but this is a coin flip between them.

6.why: Three options are extreme (sure it is wrong / indifferent / unwilling to say) and A is the lone committed-but-qualified stance, the shape that wins attitude items.

7.why: Function item: B is the only two-move option (admit, then narrow), and questioning motives / restating more strongly are stock wrong functions.

8.why: D is the general statement of the surmoulage finding that item 22's option C states in detail; the other four are consequences rather than the practice.

9.why: Only option that is both committed and specific (a warning recorded and let drop); C is the non-committal one and the rest are affect words.

10.why: B and E are a specificity twin pair (a named container in a named place); picked E because scales imply the office counter, but the pair is undecidable.

11.why: Most specific and the only functionally loaded surface (laid to a fall toward a drain); it also explains item 14's option about little coming out of the floor.

12.why: Vocab set: rejected the literal sense (reply to) on the standard in-context rule, then guessed among the three figurative senses.

13.why: Vocab set for leisure; ample time is the in-context sense and idle pastime / freedom from employment are the dictionary-first traps.

14.why: C and E are a reversal pair about how the chamber was used, and C is the loaded, evidence-bearing half (shut from outside); the other three are dating or negative claims.

15.why: Three options prescribe re-cutting and one photographs first; B alone reframes the wear as content, which items 19 and 26 corroborate as the writer's position.

16.why: All five are competing build phases; picked the two-phase structural claim, which is the usual archaeological key shape, with no support from the values.

17.why: C is the most specific narrative-source claim (somebody in the room); nothing rules out A or D.

18.why: D and A are both live; picked the committed irritation because the batch's other record items reject single-cause readings, but A is equally consistent.

19.why: Picked the option whose detail recurs elsewhere in the batch (cutting depth, item 15 option E); C is an unrelated anecdote and B is generic.

20.why: Vocab for plain; rejected the two most literal senses (easily seen, level) and guessed the character sense.

21.why: Vocab for sound; unbroken fits a structure or a stone, but sensible and reliable are equally available without the sentence.

22.why: C and E are near twins about a contaminated group; C states casts moulded off other casts, which item 8's option D states as the firm's practice.

23.why: Picked regret at her own refusal for consistency with item 30; A is the non-committal option and C contradicts the retrospective reading.

24.why: Only option that denies sufficiency without denying the effect; it is the same qualified-causation shape as item 2 option A, and B and D are its over-specified rivals.

25.why: Rule fired that the key names a motive, but B and E both name one; picked the protective motive over the promise.

26.why: E is committed on both halves (they mean well and are wrong) while C declines to decide and A, B are extremes; matches the writer's position in item 15.

27.why: Three options assert the question is settled, which would dissolve the passage's subject; picked the unresolved one, a deliberate bet on the non-adjudicating option.

28.why: A and E are a reversal pair about his expectation; picked the assumption reading over the prepared-for-refusal reading on no structural grounds.

29.why: Vocab for office; rejected the literal place sense as the trap and guessed the archaic kindness sense over proper function.

30.why: Picked the committed, specific self-criticism over B, which is this item's non-committal option; C and E are its opposites.
